Auto contrast uses shared luminance endpoints instead of independent RGB stretching, helping preserve colour. New photos start with WWE-UIE and Balanc: New photos start with WWE-UIE and Balanced after AI at 30%. Existing saved edits are kept, and you can switch off the follow-up. It analyses a small sample of the AI result and uses your dive hints for a second correction, with a separate strength starting at 30%. It reuses the AI result rather than running the model again. WWE-UIE already includes white balance, so this extra pass may overcorrect some scenes: compare neutral tones and reduce the strength or switch it off. New videos start with Five A+ sampled colour. The live camera preview stays on Balanced restoration and does not run a neural model. Video does not support this follow-up.

Processing is local; photos, videos and: Processing is local; photos, videos and custom models are not sent to an inference service. Installed web apps automatically cache the models selected in Settings. WWE-UIE, Five A+ and Shallow-UWnet are selected initially. Settings shows offline readiness and lets you download manually or switch off automatic downloads. Downloads retry missing files when connectivity returns while the app is open. Unchanged model files are reused across app updates. Browser storage can still be cleared or fill up: retain your originals and export important results. The Android APK includes all supplied models.
Source keeps frame timing and requests a: Source keeps frame timing and requests a higher bitrate; device encoding support is required. Compact reduces size. Both export 8-bit SDR.
AI video transfers sampled global colour: AI video transfers sampled global colour, not moving spatial detail or denoising. Input limits remain 10 minutes, 512 MB and about 34 MP per frame. Compact exports H.264 MP4 up to 1080p/30 fps within 256 MB, reducing bitrate for long clips. Source keeps resolution and frame timing where the device can encode them, with a bitrate target up to 36 Mbps and a 512 MB output ceiling. Its size estimate can refuse long clips instead of quietly reducing quality. Both modes process every output frame in 8-bit SDR; 4K/60 can be slow and memory-intensive. HDR working copies have already been reduced to SDR. Rotation is baked into pixels. Keep the app open; Cancel export stops processing.
JPEG High uses quality 95%; Maximum requ: JPEG High uses quality 95%; Maximum requests 99% for larger files with less compression. Browser JPEG encoding may still subsample colour; Maximum does not guarantee 4:4:4. PNG losslessly stores the rendered pixels and preserves transparency. All photo exports use the selected resolution and the current 8-bit sRGB rendering; PNG does not restore source RAW precision or Display P3 gamut.
Enabled by default for photo exports. At: Enabled by default for photo exports. Attempts to carry supported EXIF fields from JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF and DNG into the exported JPEG or PNG, including capture dates, camera/lens settings, author/copyright and GPS location when present. Turn it off for an export without source metadata. Rotation is baked into the pixels, so orientation is reset and dimensions and colour-space tags are updated. Old thumbnails, proprietary MakerNotes, XMP/IPTC, source colour profiles and unsupported tags are not copied. PNG metadata support varies between viewers. The app cannot recover metadata already removed by a gallery, sharing app or browser; this depends on the import path, not just the platform. An unreadable metadata block does not stop the photo export; a message reports the failure. Video exports can separately retain supported title, description, comment and date fields. Other container tags, HDR data and file-system dates are not guaranteed.

Android uses native CameraX capture: pho: Android uses native CameraX capture: photos use the still-camera output rather than the preview size, with supported capture metadata retained. High targets 1080p video and Standard 720p; the camera chooses supported frame rates and bitrates. Web capture uses the browser stream: High targets 1080p/30 fps at 12 Mbps, Standard 720p/30 fps at 5 Mbps. Portrait and landscape are supported. Choose 1, 3 or 5 minutes in Settings; 1: Choose 1, 3 or 5 minutes in Settings; 1 minute is the default. Recording stops at the time or file-size limit. Size and memory estimates are approximate, especially with native camera encoding. Keep the app in the foreground while recording and saving.
Camera and microphone permissions are re: Camera and microphone permissions are requested when needed. Closing releases access; backgrounding stops recording and returning restarts the preview. Closing during recording asks whether to discard it. An installed PWA can capture offline once cached. Balanced needs no model; Five A+ assist needs its model cached first. Web capture needs HTTPS or localhost. Android launcher shortcuts open Edit or Camera directly.
Five A+ assist samples the uncorrected c: Five A+ assist samples the uncorrected camera image about once a second and fits a reusable global colour change. It does not run full neural restoration on every frame. The saved photo recipe keeps this colour change for later edits; recording freezes it at the start. Red-filter and depth hints control Balanced colour when AI assist is off. Tap zoom to cycle; hold it to choose a supported zoom or lens. Ultra-wide availability depends on the device.
Camera corrects colour locally while you: Camera corrects colour locally while you shoot, starting with Balanced and offering optional Five A+ colour assist. Capture stays open after saving; close it manually to return to editing.
Scrub to inspect a frame, or play the co: Scrub to inspect a frame, or play the corrected preview without audio. Playback skips frames when processing is slow; exported video still processes every output frame. Trimming is not available yet.
